label: diffuse; weak copy-phase preference for input q / output f,z
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps) but diffuse. It leans toward the copy phase (62% of activation mass, rising late in long sequences: lift about 3.8x at t=16-17). The strongest activations, about 0.2 out of a max of 0.25, come from copy-phase steps whose input is q. Output f (8.6x lift) and output z (5.2x) are also enriched. Even so, no token or position condition gets precision above about 12%. Copy-phase input q alone: P=0.10, R=0.14. The best disjunction (input q, or output f/z, in the copy phase) reaches only F1 0.12 and mass recall 0.37 on dev. It never fires at t=0 and seldom at the delimiter. There are also scattered original-phase activations, mostly at t=2. No coherent description found.
